vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.12

The skill acts as a client for an external 'sub-agent' service (cellcog.ai) and instructs the user to weaken OpenClaw gateway security by enabling the `sessions_send` and `sessions_list` tools via a shell command in `SKILL.md`. It also facilitates reading arbitrary local files via absolute paths using `<SHOW_FILE>` tags. While these are presented as features for multi-modal analysis and asynchronous notifications, they create significant risks for data exfiltration and unauthorized session manipulation by the external service.

llm.summary: The skill's requested binaries and single API key align with its described purpose (a Python client that sends files and tasks to CellCog's API); nothing in the instructions or requirements is disproportionate, but the skill will transmit files and data off-host — so treat that as a privacy/egress risk before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description promise (any-input → any-output) matches the instructions: a Python SDK client that accepts files and multi-modal tasks. Requiring python3 and CELLCOG_API_KEY is coherent for a Python SDK that calls an external API.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to include absolute local file paths in <SHOW_FILE> tags so the SDK will read and upload those file contents to CellCog. This is expected for a multi-file processing API, but it means arbitrary local files could be transmitted if requested — a data exfiltration / privacy risk if used carelessly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec. SKILL.md suggests installing the 'cellcog' Python package via pip if needed — a normal pattern. No opaque downloads or archive extraction are present in the skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only CELLCOG_API_KEY is required, which is proportional for an external API client. No unrelated credentials or config paths are requested. Note: protecting this API key is important because it authorizes requests that can upload user data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true, does not modify other skills, and does not require elevated/system-wide persistence. Autonomous invocation is allowed (default) but is normal for skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is internally consistent and appears to do what it says: send tasks and files to CellCog via a Python SDK using CELLCOG_API_KEY. Before installing or using, consider: only provide files you are comfortable sending to an external service; do not include secrets or sensitive system files in <SHOW_FILE> tags; verify the 'cellcog' PyPI package and the vendor (cellcog.ai) if you plan to pip install it; restrict and rotate the API key if possible; check billing/credit behavior since heavy multimodal jobs can consume credits; and enable the OpenClaw 'sessions_send' gateway setting only if you trust the destination and understand where results will be delivered.
